newsitem.title: USA: Exxon La. refinery operations normal.
newsitem.headline: Exxon La. refinery operations normal.

text.p: Exxon Corp said a crude vessel bound for its Baton Rouge, La., refinery was allowed to to navigate past a barge accident that restricted shipping along the Mississippi River and its 424,000 barrel per day Baton Rouge, La., refinery was operating normally on Thursday.
"We're doing fine. The refinery is operating normally," Exxon spokesman Bruce Tackett said.
The crude tanker made its delivery late Wednesday, he said.

A Mobil Corp spokeswoman said operations at its 170,000 barrel per day Chalmette, La., refinery downstream of New Orleans were unaffected after two barge accidents and a grounded freighter shut key sections of the river.

Shipping along a section of the river at Baton Rouge is open during daylight hours to north- and south-bound traffic on a one-way, one vessel at a time basis as crews worked to lighter and upright a barge that capsized Monday.
At the mouth of the river, a grounded freighter has delayed 13 deep-draft ships and shut the river at Southwest Pass, the only river entrance for deep-draft vessels.
